\section{Type Consensus Constraint (Layer 3)}\label{app:type-consensus}

\paragraph{Motivation.}
We define a \emph{consistency-failure} (CF) violation as the case where the same entity text span receives different type labels across relation triples within a single document.
Per-relation domain/range constraints (Layer 2) operate independently on each relation and cannot enforce cross-relation type consistency.
As a result, even well-calibrated models exhibit CF rates as high as 9.90\% on SciERC under the \texttt{full\_s1} decoding mode.

\paragraph{Implementation.}
We maintain a document-level entity registry that maps each entity text to the type first assigned during decoding.
The registry is populated from the \texttt{entities} section and from head/tail types already generated in completed relation blocks.
When the decoder reaches a \texttt{head\_type} or \texttt{tail\_type} position, it queries the registry: if the corresponding entity text has a stored type, the model is forced to emit that type token.

A critical detail is \emph{domain/range-aware skipping}: if the consensus type conflicts with the allowed types for the current relation (i.e., the stored type falls outside the relation's domain or range set), the consensus constraint is not applied.
This prevents the introduction of new DR violations in exchange for resolving CF violations.

The procedure is summarized below:

\begin{enumerate}
    \item Detect that the current decoding position is an entity type field.
    \item Query the registry for the current entity text $\rightarrow$ \texttt{stored\_type}.
    \item Query the ontology for the current relation $\rightarrow$ \texttt{allowed\_types}.
    \item If \texttt{stored\_type} $\in$ \texttt{allowed\_types}: force \texttt{stored\_type}.
    \item Else: skip consensus enforcement and log a warning.
\end{enumerate}

\paragraph{Results.}
% TODO: fill with 551-doc (SciERC) + 50-doc (DocRED) full results

\begin{table}[h]
\centering
\small
\begin{tabular}{lcc}
\toprule
\textbf{Configuration} & \textbf{CF (\%)} & \textbf{DR (\%)} \\
\midrule
\texttt{full\_s1} (no GTC) & 9.90 & 0.93 \\
\texttt{full\_s1} + GTC     & ---  & ---  \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{Effect of Global Type Consensus (GTC) on consistency-failure and domain/range violation rates. % TODO: fill with 551-doc results
}
\label{tab:gtc-results}
\end{table}

Preliminary results from a 10-document dry-run confirm the mechanism works as intended: CF drops from 7.69\% to 0\%, with 3 DR-conflict skips triggered across the subset.
The DR violation rate remains at 0.0\%, improving over the baseline rate of 0.93\%.
